records.title: Insula rootfs dependency closure contract

environment.system_features: ACL GMP GNUTLS LIBSELINUX LIBXML2 MODULES NATIVE_COMP NOTIFY INOTIFY PDUMPER SECCOMP SQLITE3 THREADS TREE_SITTER ZLIB

records.mechanism: Hermetic Insula evidence is a rootfs-owned tool/package/dependency closure with ABI accounting, not merely an environment variable or a bwrap namespace.
records.hypothesis: The current development Insula should truthfully report that it uses host system binds and has no ABI guarantee; a production Soma Insula must report a selected rootfs and dependency closure.
records.minimal_fixture: The emitted `insula-plan.json' from the current run.
records.predicted_behavior: Development mode is allowed only if the plan explicitly says dependency closure is not rootfs-owned and ABI guarantee is absent.

independent_checks.name: production required tool list is recorded
rootfs dependency closure is truthfully classified

records.counterexample: Treating bwrap entry as hermetic even when `/usr' and toolchains come from the host hides unaccounted ABI and package dependencies.
records.derived_gym_requirement: Production benchmark runs must select a Soma-owned rootfs manifest before launching Emacs, LSP servers, Jupyter kernels, Comint shells, or language toolchains.

environment.system_features: ACL GMP GNUTLS LIBSELINUX LIBXML2 MODULES NATIVE_COMP NOTIFY INOTIFY PDUMPER SECCOMP SQLITE3 THREADS TREE_SITTER ZLIB

records.mechanism: The emitted bwrap plan must agree with the runtime state observed from inside Emacs.
records.hypothesis: Run id, mode, cwd, private directories, and output directory should match between environment variables, `default-directory', and `insula-plan.json'.
records.minimal_fixture: The current `insula-plan.json' plus Emacs runtime variables.
records.predicted_behavior: The plan and runtime should match for this episode, proving plan evidence is not detached from the process being probed.

independent_checks.name: private runtime directories match development sentinels

records.counterexample: A runner can emit a plausible plan and then launch Emacs with different cwd, environment, run id, or artifact paths.
records.derived_gym_requirement: The production Insula gateway must validate plan/runtime consistency before accepting Emacs, LSP, Jupyter, or checker evidence.

records.mechanism: Mount evidence must distinguish writable task/harness state, read-only configured inputs, and broad development host binds.
records.hypothesis: The current development Insula should expose a writable trace directory and private HOME while truthfully declaring host-system binds rather than rootfs-owned closure.
records.minimal_fixture: The current mount plan and several runtime-visible paths.

records.mechanism: A patched Emacs build is a distinct runtime substrate whose source, patches, build flags, executable identity, and ABI surface must be recorded before its observability evidence is trusted.

records.title: Dired undo does not restore filesystem changes

environment.system_features: ACL GMP GNUTLS LIBSELINUX LIBXML2 MODULES NATIVE_COMP NOTIFY INOTIFY PDUMPER SECCOMP SQLITE3 THREADS TREE_SITTER ZLIB

records.mechanism: `dired-undo' undoes changes in the Dired buffer; it explicitly does not recover files removed from the filesystem.
records.hypothesis: After a real file is deleted, attempting `dired-undo' should not recreate the deleted file; any undo effect is limited to Dired-buffer state.
records.minimal_fixture: One temporary directory, one file, one Dired buffer mark, and one real filesystem deletion.
records.predicted_behavior: The recovery attempt is a Dired-buffer operation; the deleted file remains absent.
records.observed_behavior: mark-before=42 undo-result=(error "(user-error \"No further undo information\")") mark-after=nil file-exists-after-dired-undo=nil

independent_checks.name: dired mark existed before filesystem deletion

records.counterexample: A generic recovery strategy that runs undo after a Dired action can fail to undo even buffer-local state and still leaves destructive filesystem state unrecovered.
records.derived_gym_requirement: Dired benchmarks must grade filesystem state independently from Dired buffer state and must classify destructive file operations as externally consequential.

records.title: with-timeout only fires at wait points

environment.system_features: ACL GMP GNUTLS LIBSELINUX LIBXML2 MODULES NATIVE_COMP NOTIFY INOTIFY PDUMPER SECCOMP SQLITE3 THREADS TREE_SITTER ZLIB

records.mechanism: `with-timeout' checks its deadline when Emacs waits for external events; CPU-bound Lisp that does not wait can run past the deadline.
records.hypothesis: A body that calls `sleep-for' should return the timeout form, while a short busy loop should run past the deadline and return normally.
records.minimal_fixture: Two short timed forms: one waiting with `sleep-for', one CPU-bound loop guarded by an outer wall-clock limit.
records.predicted_behavior: Timeout behavior differs at wait points versus CPU-bound work.

independent_checks.name: busy loop ran past timeout and returned normally

records.counterexample: In-Emacs timeouts cannot be the only watchdog for model actions or package code that can loop without waiting.
records.derived_gym_requirement: The gym supervisor needs an out-of-process watchdog, and operation results must distinguish failed, canceled, and outcome_unknown.
